reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Marsha at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said fishing for bream, crappie and catfish continues to be success this week, though crappie appear to be slowing down.
Crappie are fair now. They’ll bite minnows and jigs around brushpiles, stumps and rocky points. Catfish are good on worms and cut bait. No reports or any bass. Surface water temperature is up to 69 degrees, but the lake remains low. Park officials note that, based on “moon times,” “good” days should be falling May 28-31. Looking ahead to June, when Free Fishing Weekend for Arkansas arrives, the start of the “best” days coincides with that: June 11-17.

reports.text:
Some crappie are being caught by anglers on boats out in deeper water and using a Fish Finder, we’re told. Some of these anglers who are stopping into the shop have indicated they’ve shifted from fishing Lake Conway, which is drained for renovation, and have been finding lots of crappie willing to bite. Minnows are working best now, and reportedly some big crappie (white crappie and black crappie) are being caught.
Black bass have been “kinda slow,” she says. “I haven’t heard any reports in the last couple of weeks on bass.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Anglers have been catching a lot of bass on topwater now, as well as with worms and crankbaits. “You can catch bass now with just about anything you can get in front of them right now,” he said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth bass are fair. They can be found shallow 2-10 feet. Try using topwater, spinnerbaits, jigs, jerkbait, Chatterbait and crankbaits. Spotted bass (aka Kentucky bass ) also are fair and being found with the largemouths in 2-10 feet of water. They’ll respond to jerkbaits and jigs. In WestRock’s Tuesday night bass tournament this week, Matt Hedrick and Brandon Crain caught 11.42 pounds of bass to win, ahead of Cody Bryant and Brad Lequieu with 9.99 pounds. Matt Bryant and Garry Bryant hauled in the Big Bass of 3.46 pounds.
Crappie are good. The last report heard from anglers was that they are off the shoreline and scattered in 12 feet. Use jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are starting to be caught trolling.
Bass have slowed a bit but are still good on the lower end, such as around Big Clifty, Little Clifty and Indian Creek. Plastics are working. Tubes and Ned rigs will work.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are still in spawn and post-spawn.
(updated 5-15-2025) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) says crappie are mostly spawned out, as females are almost empty, and fish are relating back to structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be found up on the shoreline, while others are still floating around in deeper water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: The crappie spawn has come and gone as high water and fast flows prevented anglers from some great angling opportunities in the tailrace.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were good this last week, but none of the anglers let Shelly in on what they were using. We can guess that jigs and minnows were both very good, as well as worms. Crappie haven’t had a color preference of late on the jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
AGFC staff reported that bass fishing was OK this past week.
As reported by Trader Bill’s Outdoors Facebook page, though, the lake turned out ANOTHER monster black bass this past week.
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) continues to do most of his fishing at and reporting from lakes Ouachita, Hamilton and DeGray, and says, “The crappie and bass are finishing up their spawn or already in post-spawn. We are catching limits of crappie stacked up on brushpiles fished 8-12 feet deep in 18-24 feet of water.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) reports that black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still spawning a little bit but appear on the downside of it. And black bass are on fire.
Crappie are most active on minnows in 2-3 feet of water. The bass are being caught on worms, frogs, spinnerbaits and just about everything else, he said. The bass are really shallow in the lily pads.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River/Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still spawning and staying in shallow grassy areas.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass seemed to have a slump in reactions this week, with better reactions during cloud cover. With the drop of the lake pool from recent flash flooding, many bass have pulled off the shore recently, but are holding just out in the 5-10 feet zones where grass, lily pads and vegetation are present. Largemouths have been fair on square bill cranks deflecting off stumps where shallow pockets and flats drop into creek channel swings or around vertical structure with lily pads. The Bill Lewis Lures MR-6, the ATV and SB-57 crankbaits in bluegill/bream, Guacamole or Burnt Pumpkinseed patterns were working shallow the last few weeks near flats with bream beds, but this week the bass…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
AGFC staff reported that bass fishing was OK this past week.
As reported by Trader Bill’s Outdoors Facebook page, though, the lake turned out ANOTHER monster black bass this past week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
There is a good black bass bite. Largemouth bass are good. Spotted bass (aka Kentucky bass ) are also good and are found with the largemouths in 2-10 feet.
WestRock held its regular Tuesday night bass tournament this week with Josh Jeffers and Aaron Presser catching a stringer weighing 13.39 pounds, including the Big Bass of 3.94 pounds. Cody Bryant and Brad Lequieu’s five-bass stringer of 11.32 pounds was runner-up.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still in various stages of spawn, as some are up shallow and others already suspended nearing full-on summer patterns.
Bass are in the same pattern – some are on beds, while others just off the shallows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are still in all phases of the spawn.
(updated 5-8-2025) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) says crappie are mostly spawned out, as females are almost empty, and fish are relating back to structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: Some crappie are up on the bank, while others are still floating around in deeper water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said the fishing was good for most everything this past week, though there were no reports on bass (black or white) for the second week in a row. Crappie are good on worms and on jigs in all colors.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) reports that black bass are very good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: But his most recent reports had indicated that both the crappie and bass activity had been very good. Jigs and minnows work for crappie; crankbaits and spinnerbaits and some topwater should be good for bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Most largemouth bass continue roaming flats from 2-5 feet depth and appeared to be scouting areas of the oxbow lakes up Little River for bedding bream like bluegills. Largemouths have been fair to good on square-bill cranks deflecting off stumps in shallow pockets. The Stumpknocker and Sunrise Perch patterns of the Echo 1.75 size drew some reactions from 2- to 3-pound largemouth near stumps on points of the oxbows. Quarter-ounce chrome/blue Bill Lewis Spin Traps with a gold tail spinner will also grab a random reaction through fresh lily pad stems, and will connect with roaming bass.
Reactions have been very good — we’ve caught healthy 2- to 3-pound bass over the last couple weeks, and…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River/Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are spawning as normal, and the shad-colored jigs are still hot!

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Tuesday morning, one angler was using bass minnows and chicken liver on a trotline and caught six nice catfish — a couple of channel cats and some flatheads, with several ranging 3-6 pounds.
Another angler on Tuesday morning caught a nice bass from the bank on a redworm while fishing from bream.
As for crappie, one angler last week came back with a limit of crappie. Chartreuse colored jigs and crappie nibbles were working, and several catches were over 14 inches in length. But that angler was the only one that caught multiple crappie in the past week. Crappie appear to have headed into deep water and aren’t being found along the shoreline.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: “The crappie bite has picked up, with the lower end creeks producing the best bite. The crappie are spawning in the brush and trees in the back of the creeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Shelley Burr at Cane Creek State Park, (870-628-4714) said a guest at the lake caught his limit of crappie while fishing from his boat early last Thursday morning. On Saturday, they had several guests buying bait that morning for bream and crappie fishing.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fayetteville Boat Dock (479-444-3476) reports crappie were hitting well up shallow on minnows and crappie jigs. Bass should be as well, but anglers weren’t sharing specifics.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
(update 5-1-2025) Crappie guide Eric Watts of Natural State Fishing (501-548-8990) said he’s been commuting back and forth between Lake Ouachita and North Little Rock. “ We’ve been on a great crappie bite in brush in 10-20 feet of water. Casting Original Baby Shad Bobby Garland Crappie Baits in a variety of colors has produced remarkable numbers over the past three to four weeks.
Crappie can be found in 7-10 feet of water on brush and roaming in 15-20 feet of water.
“People often think crappie only bite in the spring. As we move toward summer and the weather stabilizes, crappie fishing will get even better!
Black bass are doing great. They’ve heard no reports on crappie or bream — it’s been…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“The only bright spot is on the spots, which is what I call spotted bass and, yes, pun intended. Spotted bass and smallies are on fire in the Rambo/Big Clifty and Little Clifty areas.
I assume crappie are in the process of spawning, as are the bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are in all phases of the spawn.
(updated 5-1-2025) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) says crappie are starting to get on the banks making beds where the water temperatures are more stable.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie can be found near the shoreline while some others are still floating around in deeper water.
Black bass are scattered as well.
(updated 5-1-2025) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said the lake has been fishing well as far as catching good numbers of black bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
In her most recent report, crappie fishing was doing well on minnows, and catfish were being caught using nightcrawlers on the west side of the lake.
Black bass were biting off the shoreline in fair numbers, and better out in the lake from boats. Try by the “big island” or just past it. Crappie jigs and minnows were working for the bass as well, along with crankbaits in various colors (all have gotten some action). A few bream were biting. Follow more from Harris Brake Lake Resort on its Facebook page.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Also, bream and crappie continued to be taken in good numbers by anglers for the past week. Bream are shallow now and are favoring redworms. Look for them fishing the shoreline. The bite has been good.
Crappie have been fair for the past week. Worms also are best for the crappie. No reports on black bass or white bass this week. The surface water temperature was up to 69 degrees earlier this week. The clarity remains the usual murky and the water level is still high. Fishing should be good based on the “moon times” forecast May 9-15, with the best days of this month being May 24-30. That should be the perfect time for catfish and bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) reports that black bass are still good.
Crappie are still good and relating to brush in the 8- to 20-foot range. Catfish are still good on trotlines and jugs with live and cut bait. Water temperature is gradually rising, ranging 62-68 degrees. The water clarity is clearing. The lake level Thursday was 578.12 feet msl, just slightly above normal pool. 580.75. Call the Mountain Harbor fishing guides (Mike Wurm, 501-622-7717, or Chris Darby, 870-867-7822) for more information. (updated 5-1-2025) Capt. Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) continues to do most of his fishing at and reporting…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* The largemouth bass activity has been fair to good over the past few weeks and in local tournaments. A majority of bass have been noted post-spawn, roaming shallow in search of bream beds in protected coves near cypress trees, knees and stumps from 1-4 feet deep in flats and backs of creeks in a few areas in the oxbows up Little River, where clarity is somewhat better than the river. Most bass seen roaming flats appeared to be scouting areas of the oxbow lakes up Little River for bedding bream like bluegills.
Largemouths have been fair to good on square-bill cranks deflecting off stumps in shallow pockets, especially near creeks running through flats with fresh lily pads where a creek…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River/Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still spawning, and shad-colored jigs are still bringing them in.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
When it eventually comes down, anglers can catch black bass using a wacky-rigged Senko and fish in backwaters around the grass.
Before the current ramped up and more water moved through, crappie were reacting well to black and chartreuse Crappie Magnets fished around wood of the rock piles in the backwater areas.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) continues to do most of his fishing at and reporting from lakes Ouachita, Hamilton and DeGray, and says, “The crappie and bass are finishing up their spawn or already in post-spawn. We are catching limits of crappie stacked up on brushpiles fished 8-12 feet deep in 18-24 feet of water.”
The black bass bite was OK, with the best bite coming on wacky-rigged soft-plastic worms in green pumpkin color.
“The water will be in the normal range for crappie this Thursday or Friday. The crappie have been on the bed but very difficult to get to.
The crappie spawn should still be going on.
“There was a bass tournament on DeGray on April 19.

reports.text:

We are catching limits of crappie stacked up on brushpiles fished 8-12 feet deep in 18-24 feet of water.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are doing well on buzzbaits and soft-plastic worms. Crappie are still doing well in 6-8 feet of water, but the spawn is over.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Black bass were still around 10-15 feet down, from what people have said. Crappie continue to be the top target for anglers here.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are biting on minnows and on chartreuse/black jigs.
Black bass are hitting topwater lures and crankbaits.
Still chances to stock up on crappie and others for the freezer.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie and bream.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Some are hitting the early morning or late evening wave of black bass with such lures as a Whopper Plopper, a frog or a buzzbait and working in the backwaters or around shoreline grass. On the main river, a bone-colored Zara Spook has started picking up bass there, also both early in the morning and later in the day.
Around jetties, you might also try a crankbait, while anglers also report catching some bass in the main river on a white Chatterbait, fishing it around the jetties.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are setting up toward summer areas; some are up chasing sunfish but the water rise has slowed everything.
(updated 5-30-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) reports crappie are definitely more scattered and they are finding some on the brush and structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some boaters on Saturday were using crickets, minnows for crappie and using nightcrawlers for catfish while fishing from the interior pier. Several reports surfaced from Monday’s holiday of anglers using minnows to catch crappie and bream, as well as throwing some redworms toward the bream or anything else that might bite.
One boating angler caught some crappie Tuesday fishing with minnows from his boat.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie still seem somewhat confused, like other species.
Some black bass are still spawning, more appear on their way to spawn and some have finished.
(updated 5-30-2024) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said that with all the pleasure boat traffic on the lake in the past few days (over the holiday), that had kept a lot of their usual bass angler sources away. Instead, anglers have been crappie fishing and trolling for white bass and walleye.
It’s not that you can’t fish for bass now, it’s just that the lake will be less busy and more conducive to bass early in the morning or late in the evening.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said the fishing has remained consistent over the past two weeks, with bream, crappie and catfish all biting well. Crappie are going for the usual minnows and jigs now as they are post-spawn. No reports still on bass; they’ve gone into hiding.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greeson fishing report
reports.text: Philip Kastner of Trader Bill’s Outdoors in Little Rock and Hot Springs noted on the May 21 “Wild Side Show” on KABZ-FM, 103.7 The Buzz that Greeson was a great host for the wrap up to the Trader Bill’s Team Trail schedule with a good bass bite for all the entrants, and the top three teams May 18 on Greeson were separated by just half a pound. Nathan Hall, who caught a 5-pounder just moments before the fishing was to cease and weight-in begin, teamed with Matthew Hamby for a winning 14.5 pounds of bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
The largemouth bass bite remains fair. Reports of the bass biting shallow in the mornings and evenings in 2-4 feet and others being found deeper to 8-20 feet. Spotted bass ( Kentuckies ) are also fair.
Eric Wallace and Mike Hammett netted a 5.27-pound Big Bass in Tuesday night’s black bass tourney, while Daniel Romine and Vaughn Greenway landed a 5-bass stringer of 15.38 pounds to win the event, with Randall Clark and Ben Burke catching 14.09 pounds for second.
Crappie are slow these days, though some reports have them being found suspended on brush anywhere from 12-14 feet as well as 16-21 feet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are slowly starting to move toward deeper water and can be caught 15-18 feet deep on brush piles.
(updated 5-23-2024) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Ray Hudson at River Valley Marina (501-517-1250) said the black bass are “biting like crazy,” and they’ve been biting well for a few weeks now.
One angler caught a mess of crappie this past week, all on minnows, Ray said, noting it was the first sign of crappie activity since their spawn.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass activity has been fairly consistent with last week. Recent bass tournaments on Millwood Lake in the last few weeks have weighed several bass over 9 pounds, including a few in the 10- and 11-pound class, in post-spawn condition. Many large female bass between 7-9 pounds each have been caught and released over the past few weeks. Topwater frogs, Spit’n Images, Dying Flutters, soft plastic jerkbaits, Senkos, Trick Worms, 5-inch Bass Assassin Shads and buzzbaits continue drawing reactions from 3- to 8-pound largemouths from 1-8 feet of depth at dawn and dusk.
Once the sun gets up above the treeline, switch over to a Brazalo Spinnerbait in Spot Remover, or a Bill Lewis…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: I had a client catch a smallmouth recently using a yellow Woolly Dropper.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) said anglers are catching a lot of bass, catfish and bream in recent days. Smaller bream, bass minnows, goldfish and more were all working for a good catfish, which they report were biting very well over the weekend. A crappie even bit into a goldfish and was hooked by the group.
Black bass were biting both early in the morning and late in the evening.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greeson fishing report
reports.text: Philip Kastner of Trader Bill’s Outdoors in Little Rock and Hot Springs noted on the May 21 “Wild Side Show” on KABZ-FM, 103.7 The Buzz that Greeson was a great host for the wrap up to the Trader Bill’s Team Trail schedule with a good bass bite for all the entrants, and the top three teams May 18 on Greeson were separated by just half a pound. Nathan Hall, who caught a 5-pounder just moments before the fishing was to cease and weigh-in begin, teamed with Matthew Hamby for a winning 14.5 pounds of bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Bass fish has been pretty good; they say you can catch a bunch of little Kentuckies and others. The bite is good early morning and late in the evening on topwaters like a buzzbait, Whopper Plopper and Zara Spook. During the day, crankbaits have been doing well, as well as spinnerbaits or a black and blue jig. Those have worked on the backwaters and on the main river. But know that the water is moving, and water might be up in a few places it hasn’t been. Water clarity is stained to muddy.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Spawning is done for walleye, white bass, crappie and most black ass.
Crappie will enter a period of suspension right at the thermocline that is starting to set up. Trolling will kick in for crappie the next couple of weeks.
Black bass will also set up on humps and points, same depth as walleye.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are for the most part post-spawn — some are up chasing sunfish but the rise has everything slowed.
(updated 5-23-2024) Crappie 101 Guide Service (870-577-2045) reports crappie are definitely more scattered and they are finding some on the brush and structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Teresa Atchley at Cane Creek State Park (870-628-4714) said Cane Creek Lake saw fishing for crappie, bream, catfish and anything else that might bite by its anglers this past week. Saturday, anglers were tossing crickets and caught bream and crappie, with nightcrawlers picking up catfish and minnows and redworms getting action from a variety of fish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Bates Field and Stream (501-470-1846) said crappie, catfish and bream are all biting well by the Highway 89 bridge. Black bass are hitting crankbaits and topwater round the lake.
Crappie are favoring minnows as well as black/chartreuse or pink/white jigs.
Still chances to stock up on crappie and others for the freezer.
The pond is more than 60 acres and has bass, crappie and bream.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie seem somewhat confused, as with the other species.
Black bass are prespawn, spawning or have finished.
Topwater fishing has been good for black bass and there are schooling fish.
The crappie on Greers has somewhat slowed down.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Bream, crappie and catfish all continue to bite well. Black bass still continue to stay out of sight.
Crappie are hitting jigs and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Whether it’s the storms this week, the spawn being over or something else, the largemouth bass bite has slowed. and all fishing has been slow other than the fair bream bite. Reports from the lake have largemouths now in post-spawn and starting to move out to 8-20 feet. Spotted bass ( Kentucky bass ) also are slow.
This past Tuesday’s black bass tournament showed a slight falloff in weights, too. Matt Hedrick and Brandon Crain won the event with a 5-bass stringer of 13.32 pounds, edging Andrew Wooley and Cameron Nesterenko by 0.15 pound. Brent Scott and Riley Scott netted the Big Bass of 4.44 pounds.
Crappie are slow. Some reports of crappie being found suspended on brush anywhere from 16-21…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been good, “everybody’s catching bass,” Ray says. “They are catching big bream as well. Bream are on their beds.” Black bass are biting on spinnerbaits and soft plastic worms. Bream are great on crickets and live worms. Ray said he had not heard much on the crappie. “It appears the crappie are fizzing out. Some anglers are catching a few, but it’s not great.” But catfish are biting well, he noted. Blues and channels are hungry, with liver and hot dogs being the best presentations.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass activity has been fairly consistent and with not much change this week from last week. Bream and crappie fishing remained good, and catfish are really taking off with excellent results this past week.
Use worms, crickets jigs for a great bream bite now, while minnows and jigs are preferred by crappie, along with Arkie Gill Candy.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth bass are biting fair to good. Reports of the bass being found on points around 10 feet deep. Spotted bass (Kentucky bass) are biting fair, with some reports of them being found near 10 feet and off rocky points. The bass were biting well for the Tuesday night anglers in the weekly black bass tournament on Maumelle, with 22 boats competing and 19 of them catching limits. First place with a 5-bass weight of 15.11 pounds was the team of Vaughn Greenway and Daniel Romine, who also hauled in the Big Bass of 5.48 pounds.
Crappie are fair. Reports of crappie hanging in the brush around 18 ft of water. Try using white Bobby Garland jigs, or minnows. Bream are biting fair to good. Reports…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text:
Sheila Ferrebee, the new owner of Carter Cove Bait Shop and More (479-272-4025), formerly Andrews, says crappie, bream and catfish all are biting well. Some of the crappie are in the 2-pound range, and two cats that were pulled from the lake this week “were the biggest I’ve seen,” she said. “We’ve been going through crickets like crazy for the bream and the crappie.” Black bass are biting “pretty good” on jigs and minnows. Crappie are also biting biting minnows and white jigs.
(updated 5-11-2023) Ken Winstead at Whiskers Sporting Goods (501-889-2011) in Perryville said the crappie bite continues to be typical for the continuous water changes due to weather, so move around from shallow to…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said crappie are still on the brushtops in 20-28 feet ft water fished 8-12 feet deep.
(updated 5-25-2023) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are good.
Crappie are good and being caught on small jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
The black bass seem to be right up on the banks as well and appear to be at or toward the end of spawning.
Not much news on the crappie end; some were caught this week but they weren’t great, Ray said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass are fair to good, best early and late, ranging 2-3 pounds in 3-8 feet of water on flats near vegetation, and others in 6- to 10-feet deep creek channels where grass and reeds and fresh lily pad shoots are emerging. Brazalo Spinnerbaits, lizards, Bass Assassin Shads and Chatterbaits are working. Over the past couple weeks, largemouths have been randomly feeding in creek channels dumping into Little River. A few chunky 2- and 3-pound bass were the most aggressive early into late morning over the past week and those fish are being found randomly near deeper creek channels or ditches through the flats. The best bass activity is shifting from midday to early morning on…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: Spawned-out crappie are on brush about 5-10 feet down and feeding on live minnows on slip floats and jigs cast over the brush and allowed to sink into it. Black bass are also biting near the bank on crankbaits. The smallmouth bite is over.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Sheila Ferrebee, the new owner of Carter Cove Bait Shop and More (479-272-4025), formerly Andrews, says crappie, bream and catfish all are biting well. Some of the crappie are in the 2-pound range, and two cats that were pulled from the lake this week “were the biggest I’ve seen,” she said. “We’ve been going through crickets like crazy for the bream and the crappie.” Black bass are biting “pretty good” on jigs and minnows. Crappie are also biting minnows and white jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text:
Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) says crappie limits are being caught, and good-sized crappie at that. The crappie started back up about two weeks ago and anglers are catching a bunch daily. “Every crappie we see, they’re hungry,” we’re told.
Nothing reported on bass lately.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been coming around on live worms as well, with bass being found mostly off the pier and relatively shallow. Crappie have been steady and the ones being caught are about 10 inches or bigger. Bream and crappie are the most prominent catches now, they report.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: “Crappie are moving back into the brush piles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie have slowed down a little, but there still biting in 8-10 feet of water. Bass are chasing the little fry that are everywhere. Catfish are being caught on jugs, limb lines and trotlines using perch or bass minnows.
Crappie are hiding in the brush piles. Bass are hit and miss, “but the recent bass tournament I saw out here would make me think they are still active,” Lacey added.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth bass are starting to get active with the spawn over. The smallmouth are all in the river, you’ve just got to fish for them deep.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: Lake Erling Guide Service (870-904-8546) says crappie are getting back out and are scattered in the deeper water, but they are biting well still. There are some people looking for bass but they are not checking in to say what they’ve caught.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Early in the morning or late in the evening, bass are biting a black or white buzzbait as well as a frog.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are shallow to suspended deep.
Bass should be in full spawn mode.
Anglers are catching good numbers of crappie but they are having to search for them and many of the caught crappie are reported to be under the slot limit and returned to the water. Largemouth bass have been pretty decent for anglers fishing the creeks and streams, catching them on their beds, in tributaries and up real shallow on presentations such as a Ned rig.
Beaver Lake was described as “pretty muddy” up until a few days ago around Monte Ne, with fishing not that good in that area, but up further north in the lake, anglers were reported fishing with Kastmasters on a Sunday and were catching 30-40 bass, using…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass have been in prespawn. Crappie reportedly are starting to get more active. Crappie will favor the live stuff, particularly No. 6 size crappie minnows.
(update 4-27-2023) AGFC biologists have recently sampled Brewer Lake and seem some very positive results concerning black bass. The high water at Brewer Lake is in the bushes now, and so are the bass. A 6-pound, 5-ounce bass was sampled near the south boat ramp and in slightly deeper water than most others.
On a second night of sampling Brewer, more quality largemouth bass and crappie were collected off the south bank along the main lake along the water willow line.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: With warmer temperatures the smallmouths are more active.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are up close to the shoreline and doing well. Trick Worms in a June bug color, frogs, Rooster Tails and about any other kind of favored bass baits are working right now. Crappie are out on the flats. Lake Conway crappie usually are interested in jigs in white and chartreuse, Monkey Milk, anything with orange in it – generally your brighter colors to get their attention in the usual Conway stain.
Nightcrawlers, Catfish dip, any Catfish Magic type of bait, little bream for the flatheads, trotline minnows and bass minnows for the lines, and goldfish will catch them.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: However, before the recent conditions, he says, crappie had still not moved in and haven’t spawned. Some anglers reported to him that the water temperature earlier this week was 76 degrees and that the temperature might need to drop to see crappie shallow. As for black bass, anglers were catching lots of those recently, particularly near the lower end of the lake, on spinnerbaits and frogs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
That rise got all the fish active: black bass, crappie, catfish and bream. Anglers were catching white crappie with black jigs and ghost bottoms, and they were catching crappie bream AND catfish on crappie jigs. It was reported to Shelly that crappie are in full spawn now.
Bass reports were good, but Shelly not no word on the baits. Catfish were biting well on blood bait and stink bait. Bream are good on worms, crickets and jigs in all colors. The water is its usual murky clarity and is at a normal level.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fayetteville Boat Dock (479-444-3476) reported that anglers have been having a lot of success out crappie fishing on usual crappie baits (minnows, jigs).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said crappie are in post-spawn, “meaning they are finished making babies and are hungry. We have caught ample numbers of large crappie in a wide variety of environments ranging from 8-16 feet deep on brush piles in 18-28 feet of water. The bass are finishing their spawn and the catfish are moving up into the shallower water.”
(updated 5-11-2023) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are still good. Crappie are fair and still being caught on small jigs or minnows.
One of his anglers went out Wednesday morning and said it was like going back in time to 2½ weeks ago and was…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass were doing really well before the rain.
Crappie seemed to be tapering off, asthe spawn seems about done there.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Most largemouth bass have completed their spawning activities over the past several weeks in the oxbows and many are now post-spawn up Little River. Males and female Largemouths, from 2-3 pounds and up to 9 pounds as recently as last week, have been caught shallow, in 1-3 feet of water on flats near vegetation, and others in 6-9 feet deep creek channels where grass and reeds and fresh lily pad shoots are emerging. Brazalo spinnerbaits, lizards, Bass Assassin Shads and Chatterbaits are working. Over the past couple weeks, Largemouths have been randomly feeding in creek channels dumping into Little River. A few chunky 2- and 3-pound male Bass, were the most aggressive at midday into late…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Some bass and crappie are still spawning, but many have finished. Both spawned-out bass and crappie are moving on brush piles and under docks. The topwater bite is getting good early at sunrise and lasts longer on cloudy days, and another is in the evening but is mostly bass partway back in the windblown creeks.
Smallmouth bass are on shallow flats and around points on creature baits.
Crappie are both on brush and scattered out in coves roaming between brush. Bass are on shoreline points in 3-10 feet of water. I have found also some nice bass feeding in the middle of a cove in 30 feet of water. I was trolling for crappie with four rods out and all four got hammered by bass at the same time…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: On Saturday, there was a little smallmouth bite in the current of the big river just in front of the creek, biting white maribou Trout Magnets.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass have been in prespawn. Crappie reportedly are starting to get more active. Crappie will favor the live stuff, particularly No. 6 size crappie minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass were caught even Thursday morning in the rain, though, right up near the bait shop in shallow water. Some decent-sized bream have been caught on crickets in the shallower areas of the lake, particularly around Crappie Cove and Doughty Cove, two of the shallower spots. Crappie is still not producing of late, they say.
Black bass are doing well.
Crappie are biting and typical for all this changing water with the weather, so move around from shallow to deep water. There is a Crappie Magnet bite, and make sure to try to with minnows and nightcrawlers, too.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Poinsett fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, while catch-and-release only, have been hammering pink and chartreuse jigs. Bass continue to do well on crankbaits and shallow-water baits, and they also are catch-and-release only.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Another wave of bass have moved up, we got another big wave. There’s a shad spawn with post-spawner bass feeding.
The bass are definitely grouping up.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text:
Bass fishing has picked up with the spawn winding down.
Crappie fishing is really good as the spawn is winding down. Natural colors such as Monkey Milk and live minnows are working very well. Many crappie actually are being caught on bass lures, such as structure bugs or rage bugs. They’re catching crappie in 6-10 feet of water, with some being caught around floating mats, jetty rocks and brush pads.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hiding in the brush piles. Bass are hit and miss, “but the recent bass tournament I saw out here would make me think they are still active,” Lacey added.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) reports that for black bass in the backwaters, mostly anglers have been using a Texas-rigged black/blue creature bait or a Texas-rigged Strike King Structure Bug in a summer craw color.
Crappie on the river have been biting in the entrances to the backwaters.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“ Crappie will either start to spawn or, as I have seen, unfortunately pull back and start to adsorb eggs.
Bass fishing will be a shallow proposition.
Monday and Tuesday, the crappie fishing was good for reporting anglers.
Black bass have been about the same as crappie, they say.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie reports from the daytime anglers aren’t coming in now, but crappie are being caught late at night on yo-yos.
Black bass are starting to hit the shoreline too.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are everywhere: up shallow, out roaming and deep on structure. Black bass are pretty much same as crappie. Spinnerbaits, topwater, crankbaits, Alabama rigs, drop-shots, Carolina rigs, Texas rigs, spoons – a lot is going on every day, some bass still spawning, a big shad spawn is going on in different places, and with weather forecasts it looks like the same all this month as well.
There are a lot of different ways you can catch bass now, they say.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are doing well.
Crappie are biting and typical for all this changing water with the weather, so move around from shallow to deep water. There is a Crappie Magnet bite, and make sure to try to with minnows and nightcrawlers, too.
(updated 4-27-2023) Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says crappie are still slow, not what they expect there for this time of year. A few caught some black bass on the bank. Also, some people have caught a few catfish on trotlines and noodles baited with either bass minnows or baby bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine Tailwater (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: The crappie spaw n is still underway, and these fish can be caught with live minnows and jigs fished in current breaks around sandbars and rock structure. Crappie shy away from heavy current and thrive in protected areas out of the main flow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text:
Anglers are catching crappie and panfish on jigs, crickets and minnows, as well as with worms. Both the bream bite and crappie bite are good. Crappie seem to be around the shoreline and in 6-8 feet of water.
No reports on black bass or white bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) said crappie are finishing their spawn and are really beginning to stack on the brush piles. “Observations around the fish cleaning stations let me know ample numbers of spotted bass are being caught and the catfish are obviously starting to move up.”
One of his anglers went out Wednesday morning and said it was like going back in time to 2½ weeks ago and was catching bass on a floating worm right in front of buckbrush and on a topwater bait.
(updated 5-4-2023) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out-of-state) said black bass are still good. Crappie are fair to good Catfish are very good on jugs and…

reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Most largemouth bass have completed their spawning activities over the past several weeks in the oxbows and many are now post-spawn up Little River. Brazalo Spinnerbaits, lizards, Bass Assassin Shads and Chatterbaits are working. Over the past couple weeks, largemouths have been randomly feeding in creek channels dumping into Little River.
A few chunky 2- and 3-pound male bass were the most aggressive at midday into late afternoon over the past couple weeks and those fish were being seen randomly near deeper creek channels or ditches through the flats. The best bass activity is shifting from midday to early morning on buzzbaits, Chatterbaits in chartreuse Sexy Shad and black/blue in dingy…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The bass fishing improved earlier this week and needed to. Some crappie are spawning, some have spawned and some are staging. Some bass are on beds but not a lot.
Bass are around shallow points on both sides near brush and swimbaits, grubs, Gitzits and creature baits are all catching fish.
Crappie are both on brush and scattered out in coves roaming between brush. Bass are on shoreline points in 3-10 feet of water. I have found also some nice bass feeding in the middle of a cove in 30 feet of water. I was trolling for crappie with four rods out and all four got hammered by bass at the same time. I have also found bass in 25 feet deep brush piles.
“Another angler landed some nice striped…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greeson fishing report
reports.text: Philip Kastner of Trader Bill’s Outdoors in Little Rock and Hot Springs said on the weekly “Wild Side Show” on KABZ-FM, 103.7 The Buzz that the crappie bite on Greeson. If you want to go crappie fishing, he says that for the last week everybody he knows that fishes for crappie is done by 8 a.m. You don’t have to brush pile fish right now for crappie on Greeson.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Ken Winstead at Whiskers Sporting Goods (501-889-2011) in Perryville said the crappie bite continues to be typical for the continuous water changes due to weather, so move around from shallow to deep water. Also throw Crappie Magnet, minnows and nightcrawlers. Black bass are doing well on dark colors, as well as watermelon red, red or blue shad, and minnows and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“I have no new info on black bass or bream.
“ Crappie can still be caught on jigs and minnows in the brush piles.
We have a full moon coming up and the last round of bass that didn’t spawn on last full moon are roaming the shallows as we speak. Been seeing several bass ranging anywhere from 1-pound buck males to quite a few over 7 pounds. These bass can be caught on a fluke, a wacky worm and a Texas-rigged lizard.
“I’ve also noticed a few more crappie have moved up shallow on some beds as well. Bream are roaming the shallows attacking the bass beds for eggs and small fry. Crappie can still be caught on brush 8-10 feet deep, as well as some shallower.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are fair on minnows and super jigs in green and chartreuse colors. Fish for crappie off the rock jetties on the main river. Black bass are biting well on black buzzbaits around the rock jetties.
Two weeks ago, when they had a moment to get on the river, black bass were good off the ends of jetties, with anglers using shaky heads and Zoom Trick Worms in green pumpkin, as well as Strike King 3XD in citrus shad color.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are in the backs of arms that contain some clearer water. I have heard reports from 5 feet to trolling cranks and crappie suspended at 12-15 feet of water.
Crappie are fair, with best action along the shoreline. Black bass are good using wacky worms, small worms or drop-shot worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are experience good fishing for most pecies, with the crappie biting fair. Crappie are being caught in 6-7 feet depth by trolling and spider-rigging down the channel or over underwater brushpiles; use minnows or jigs. Black bass are good in the evenings when it’s warmer; use a spinnerbait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: With warmer temperatures, the smallmouths are active.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass have started taking the hook. Anglers are catching good bass using spinnerbaits, crankbaits and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remain fair. Black bass are good around lily pads and grassy areas.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair, with a few here and there. Black bass are fair, but no specific baits were suggested.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are scattered all over with a lot holding in the old brush line. Crappie are chewing on minnows and jigs, all over the lake and rivers super shallow out to 40 feet as well.
(updated 5-26-2022) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said black bass are good in flooded buckbrush on flukes and white spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie, on the other hand, are poor. Black bass picked back up and started taking to minnows and usual bass lures in good numbers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Erling fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and are in deeper water. Black bass are schooling on shallow points chasing shad.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were fair on minnows and jigs. No reports on black bass or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Bass (especially largemouth) have been “on go” the last few weeks. Bass have taken up positions in semi-deep waters (14-25 feet) on points and structure near current, like brushpiles, bridges and docks. Jigs, drop-shot rigs with mainly a fluke or a drop-shot worm in green pumpkin have put lots of good, healthy largemouth and chunky spotted bass in the baot during daylight hours. When night starts to fall, and darkness sets in, the bass are just as good in very shallow areas and flats.
Crappie and bream have been decent lately with the two species mixed in and suspended over brush and under deeper docks at 12-22 feet. A live minnow is always good in the morning and evenings and jigs in…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) said bass are good in 10-15 feet depth on drop-shots and Carolina rigs.
Fishing for black bass is good. Largemouth bass are good. Reports of the bass being found shallow along the grass lines. Kentucky bass are good. Cameron Nesterenko and Andrew Wooley won Tuesday night’s black bass tournament with a five-bass haul of 15.33 pounds, which included a 5.46-pound Big Bass. Four duos caught at least 10.5 pounds of bass. Caleb Yielding caught a 3.98-pound bass, which was the second best bass caught Tuesday night.
Crappie are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are being found in 8-10 feet depth and around brushpiles, with minnows and black/chartreuse jigs still your best bets. Black bass are fair, and anglers are having their best success with Zoom Worms while fishing off points on the original shoreline.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
“We’re still catching crappie but with all the weather changes, they don’t know if they want to be shallow (fish minnows 8 feet deep in 15 feet of water on brushpiles) or deeper near even deeper channels (fish minnows or jigs 14 feet deep on 24 feet of water on brushpiles).
They report that bass are good in the grass on Texas-rigged Senkos or shallow-running square-bill crankbaits.
(updated 5-26-2022) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) said black bass are still good. Crappie are good on small jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Bass are dling well on crankbaits, buzzbaits and plastic worms. Crappie are out in the deeper water and some anglers are catching limits. Catfish are cranking up on trotlines and jigs baited with bass minnows and perch.
Crappie are out deeper; use minnows. Bass are still loving the beetle spins up in the shallows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair; they are moving off of the shoreline and are still interested in both minnows and jigs. Black bass are good, with artificial baits working.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows. Black bass are found in shallow water and the bite has been good this week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass are fair to good, most activity in oxbows up Little River, early and late in the day. Bass are moving horizontally out to deeper water during heat of the afternoons, and shallow to cover early and late. Bass are fair to good on top water lures around emerging new Lily Pad stands and vegetation at daylight. We continue seeing 3- to 4-pound bass, running in and out of shallow flats early for the past few weeks, and will bust a buzzbait, topwater chugger, and plastic frogs in the pads early. reports.text: Bass have been doing pretty well with the water temps being in this predator’s wheel house.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River/Clarendon Area fishing report
reports.text: We tried fishing for crappie near brush in the sloughs and just off main channels but got no bites.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are doing like they are in most locations in the region: moving back into deeper water with the spawn now over. Black bass are fair; try spinnerbaits, topwater baits and Chatterbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, with minnows, jigs, hand-tie jigs and crankbaits all bringing them in. Black bass are good.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Great news for future crappie structure but it is creating lots of debris throughout.
Crappie are beginning to suspend in and around 15 feet. Bass are setting up on points.
Crappie also were fair; they were being caught deeper over recent days using crankbaits or minnows. Black bass catching is good; your best bet is going with spinnerbaits, wacky worms, jerkbaits and wake baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: A few Kentucky bass were caught with soft plastics, throwing at structure and working the shorelines.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are elusive, but there is a fair amount being caught on minnows for some anglers. Black bass are favoring plastic worms with good results.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
“The other good news is that the crappie have returned to the brushpiles.
Darryl Morris at Family Fishing Trips DeGray says crappie have completed their spawn and the spotted bass are finishing.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are still spawning in lake, and some also in rivers and small creeks; use jigs or minnows and or a beetle spin for best bite. Black bass are still spawning while some guarding nests and some headed out to deeper water.
(updated 5-13-2020) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood says smallmouth bass continue to bite well on the peanut butter and jelly jig on the edges of bushes, and they’re also hitting the Carolina-rig in 10-20 feet of water. Topwater baits also are working on the smallmouth. Largemouth bass also will hit a PBJ jig on the edge of bushes. Crappie are favoring beetle spins around the bushes on the upper end of the lake.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass are being found around the shoreline and are biting well on spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Catherine (Below Carpenter Dam) fishing report
reports.text: Most of the year had been lost to fishing due to the flooding in January and February, which interfered with the crappie and walleye spawning times.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: “I am hearing that crappie fishing is tough this season as many anglers are finding smaller crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass reports are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text:
Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said bass fishing has been good early in the mornings.
pumpkin, green pumpkin and watermelon/red are hot baits for Norrell bass right now. Crappie seem to have gone deep again and the bite has slowed. In the accompanying photo, Dallas Curtis and Bob Elrod caught some nice bass in Lake Norrell fishing plastic worms wacky-style.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that the black bass bite is good. Crappie are very good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Before the past week’s heavier rainfall, fishing had stayed about same for a two-week period, with bream being caught in good numbers in 2 feet depth on worms and crickets, black bass biting spinnerbaits, crankbaits and soft plastic worms, and catfish were going after chicken liver or minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
* Largemouth bass: They improved over the past week on Millwood, many now post-spawn and recovering, upriver and in many locations. Best water clarity is in the back of oxbows but Bass are somewhat less finicky than the past few weeks, with what they are responding to. Buzzbaits, Frogs, Bass Assassin Shads, & Crazy Shads have gotten good reactions from Bass lately. Most Largemouths continue to recover from the spawning activities upriver in the oxbows of McGuire, Mud, and Horseshoe Lakes. In the creek channels near the golf course pockets between Millwood State Park and South Hickory, Largemouth Bass improved and were busting top water baits early.
Bass Assassin Shads, and soft plastic…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Peckerwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair; most anglers were trolling and spider-rigging and using minnows and jigs. She hears that black bass are good, but no baits were mentioned.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie fishing has been slow this week and all reports have been of small fish hitting small minnows. Bass have been biting minnows, black salties, watermelon/red plastic worms and Kalin’s Grubs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said bass fishing has been good early in the mornings. Wacky-rigged Zoom Zlinkys, Trick Worms and Carolina-rigged lizards in pumpkin, green pumpkin and watermelon/red are hot baits for Norrell bass right now. Crappie seem to have gone deep again and the bite has slowed.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still biting fair for some but have moved back out to deep water. Minnows, Bobby Garland Slab Slayer Jigs and Beaver Bottom Jigs in black/chartreuse are doing a pretty good job right now. Bass have been biting wacky-rigged worms, Carolina-rigged worms, lizards and Brush Hogs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The bass are also feeding and with this week’s upcoming weather pattern we should see an explosion of fish activity.
The crappie are still deep and they are being caught trolling flicker shad over deep brushpiles.
The crappie bite continues to be good and there are still several different fishing methods to catch them, he said. “I have been trolling the Berkley Flicker Minnow, size 7 and 9. Colors vary by day, but I have had success with the following; slick pearl silver, racy shad, slick Firetiger and slick alewife. The crappie that I have been finding are back in coves and the fish are on brush or near the brush suspended 15-25 feet down. The brush can be in 20-40 feet of water, as long…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Bass were biting minnows, crawfish, Zoom Lizards and Baby Brush Hogs, Zing Tail Spinners and crawfish crankbaits. Crappie fishing was fair with No.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has been slow. Bass have been biting pretty well on minnows and soft plastics like Zoom Trick Worms, lizards and Brush Hogs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River at Morrilton fishing report
reports.text: “You get back up in some of the creeks, like Point Remove Creek, get back in that when the water is not flowing and the fish are around the wood structure, they are catching largemouth bass on shallow-running crankbaits in various colors – chartreuse, orange with black – and spinnerbaits. Also on the Petit Jean River when water flow isn’t too high on the river, anglers have been catching both bream and crappie on redworms. Crappie are also biting jigs in chartreuse/black or chartreuse with red heads and dark-colored skirts, he said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: A random crappie or two can be caught, Del says; minnows or jigs will work. Black bass are good on topwater baits such as Zara Spooks, as well as poppers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
The bass are also feeding and with this week’s upcoming weather pattern we should see an explosion of fish activity.
The crappie are still deep and they are being caught trolling flicker shad over deep brushpiles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: War Eagle Creek/Beaver Lake Area fishing report
reports.text: Loy Lewis with War Eagle Creek Outfitting (479-530-3262) says smallmouth bass are biting excellent this week from Withrow State Park/Arkansas Highway 23 North bridge access to War Eagle Mill area on live worms or plastic worms. In Big Clifty arm and the Rambo area of Beaver Lake, Kentucky bass fishing is excellent in the clear-water portions and some white bass have been caught in the Hogs Scald area, along with excellent flathead catfishing using perch.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: The crappie spawn appears to be done, and the bite is good on minnows and jigs. Black bass were active again this week with a good bite on spinnerbaits, topwater lures and Chatterbaits all are working.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: They hear good news on the crappie front, with good catches targeting 5-8 feet depth using Beaver Bottom bait (Ashdown Smackdown in blue/chartreuse and black/chartreuse). Also, black bass reports are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass can be caught in good numbers with spinnerbaits, crankbaits, plastic worms, frogs, chatterbaits and buzzbaits.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are doing well on crankbaits and plastic worms. Some crappie are being found in 3 feet of water and others in 6 feet depth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
They hear good news on the crappie front, with good catches targeting 5-8 feet depth using Beaver Bottom bait (Ashdown Smackdown in blue/chartreuse and black/chartreuse). Also, black bass reports are good.
Crappie can be found active in the backwaters. Black bass are also biting in the backwaters.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs. The crappie are scattered from shallow buckbrush to 40 feet deep. “I caught many limits of nice-size crappie on structure in 30-40 feet of water last week. The fish I have been catching look to be reabsorbing eggs for some reason. Eggs were white and mushy. On the other hand I have been catching very large females in 3 feet of water full of mature healthy eggs. My advice is, do not pass up your deeper structure as those places are holding nice-size crappie.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: Kentucky bass are being caught between Beaver and Holiday Island throwing suspended hard baits and soft plastics. Most of the bass are being caught in 10-14 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: A few crappie have been reported off of No. 6 crappie minnows. Bass have been good off of crawfish and plastics.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows. Not a lot of people are talking about the bass, they say, but they see good catches and anglers are catching a lot of smaller fish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Darryl Morris at Family Fishing Trips says the crappie have had a long and hard spawn loosing allot of weight but they got the job done. Water temps are in the low 70s so the catfish are moving up.. hang on and set the drag right on that crappie pole.
“Still seeing bass on the beds in the clearer water around Iron Mountain Area. Bass fishermen are catching fish on lots of baits. The buckbrush is loaded with bass, both Kentucky bass and largemouths.
Crappie are still in the brushpiles. The crappie are gathered in clouds over the piles. The problem is that many piles are loaded with 8-inch crappie. However, if you can find the right one, it will be loaded with big crappie.
